title: Visible Tabs
prompt: A React tab bar receives every possible tab but should render only the visible ones. Write a helper that returns the labels for tabs where hidden is not true.

explanation.beginner:
Example: visibleTabs([{"label":"Home"},{"label":"Admin","hidden":true},{"label":"Profile"}]) produces ["Home","Profile"]. Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Compare “handles all hidden tabs”: input [[{"label":"Admin","hidden":true}]] produces []. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Tempting mistake: Selecting a display position after a list changes can identify the wrong item. Use the domain key when matching two collections.

The reference uses filter, map. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles all hidden tabs”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
